A formally verified, physically evaluated reinforcement-learning environment for RTL optimization.

Verilog RTLVerilatorYosys equivalenceOpenROADNangate45KLayoutPythonClaude API

1Features

  • Verification-gated reward: Verilator simulation, then Yosys sequential equivalence, then OpenROAD RTL-to-GDS; unverified designs score -1000
  • Decomposed formal proofs for reduction trees: 0.38 s per design instead of 70+ minutes
  • Content-addressed, bit-reproducible evaluations (RTL, flow, container and tool versions hashed)
  • Query-budgeted RL environment with duplicate rejection, exact replay and frozen-policy controls
  • Tool-using agent environment for Claude: simulate, prove, estimate, budgeted place-and-route
  • Stage-proxy screening: floorplan timing ranks designs with rho 0.97 at 15% of tool time
  • Measured noise floor: comment-only edits left 13 of 14 designs bit-identical; null edits are scored as ties
  • 1,752 routed designs, 15 benchmark widths and families, 20+ preregistered studies

4Findings

Reward hacking on day one

5 of 10

Under a loose testbench, every spec-violating 8-bit adder beat its correct twin by dropping the output-hold enable (10 to 15% less area). Sequential equivalence against a reference now gates every reward.

Verification that scales

11,142x faster

Proving a 16-lane adder tree against a sequential accumulator has no shared internal signals, so SAT stalls. Cut-point proofs plus a 47-step rewrite certificate prove it in seconds and still reject 7 of 7 injected bugs.

Proxy rewards for EDA latency

rho 0.97

Static timing at the floorplan stage predicts the post-route ranking across 1,752 designs; synthesis area alone does not (median rho 0.00). It is a screen, not an oracle: it ranked the most novel adder 40th of 116, while screening after global placement kept the true best in 15/15 benchmarks.

RL under controls

2 better, 2 worse, 20 tied

Hierarchical REINFORCE beat a factorized one on fresh adder widths, but identical frozen policies matched it. I fixed a policy-gradient bias from rejection sampling and traced the real limit to search coverage.

Claude as an RTL agent

15/36 vs 9/36

Episodes that beat the baseline by more than the flow's noise floor, with cheap verification and estimate tools versus place-and-route alone, over 72 episodes with Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5 and Opus 5. Opus wrote registered popcount trees up to +2.02 and a Ling adder that beat all prior search. Agents also found two holes: null edits that leave the netlist unchanged moved scores by -0.0865 to +0.0304, and Opus's top score (+5.01) retimed logic past the output register, a rule the checkers never enforced. Both are now flagged.

7Notes

Open 45 nm library and the OpenROAD flow: no commercial tools, multi-corner signoff, activity-based power or tapeout.

Blocks are small (tens to about a thousand cells) at low utilization and a 10 ns clock. The reward, 10 x WNS - 0.001 x area, is a proxy that weights slack heavily.

RL studies use 3 random seeds per condition and 16-query budgets: enough to falsify large claims, not to measure small effects.

"Formally verified" means proven sequentially equivalent to a reference module, not timing or physical signoff.
